utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-04-83-T, The Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis, did you want to say something before I carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to take a seat. Thank you very much. Before Mr. Mundis stands up again, the Chamber would like to render an oral decision in one of the motions filed by the Prosecution. The Trial Chamber renders its decision on the Prosecution motion for leave to amend its exhibit list filed on 30th October, 2007. In its motion, the Prosecution requests leave to amend its Rule 65 ter exhibit list by adding the remaining pages of the expert report of Sabiha Silajdzic-Brkic, pages 1 to 8 of the report in B/C/S and the English translation of the corresponding portion have already been admitted into evidence as Exhibit 654. The Prosecution also seeks permission to recall Sabiha Silajdzic-Brkic in less than 30 days from the date of its motion. The Defence, in its response, on the 2nd of November, 2007, does not oppose the motion. The Trial Chamber has considered the arguments advanced by the Prosecution in its motion. Trial Chamber notes that on 29 October 2007 it ordered Sabiha Silajdzic-Brkic to be recalled and that her further appearance is now scheduled for 21 November 2007. The Trial Chamber finds that it is in the interests of justice to allow the addition of the requested material to the Prosecution exhibit list and to allow her being recalled to complete her testimony within 30 days from the date of the motion. Pursuant to Rule 54 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The motion is therefore granted. Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis, you are now allowed to stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just as a creature of habit, Your Honour, I expected that you would ask for the appearances earlier and that's why I was on my feet. I don't know if that's necessary or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because you stood up, you made me skip that part of it by mistake. I'm very sorry. Now even Mr. Robson is standing now. Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to interrupt introductions, but as we were just dealing with a housekeeping matter before my colleague Madam Vidovic mentioned another matter which I'd just like to raise before the Trial Chamber. I could do it now or I could do it after the introductions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's do the introductions. I'm sorry to have messed up the procedure this afternoon. Let's have appearances, then, starting with the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager Alma Imamovic-Ivanov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my learned friends from the Office of the Prosecutor. To all those in and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Delic with legal assistant Lejla Gluhic and with us with have our intern Raymond Byrnes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Did you have something to raise Mr. Mundis? Okay, Mr. Robson, you had something to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I just wanted to let the Trial Chamber know that on the 31st of October, the Prosecution filed the Prosecution 4th motion for leave to amend its exhibit list. That was a motion that pertains to a Prosecutor by the name of Muris --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A Prosecutor by the name of Muris.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: -- Hadziselimovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: A Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes. A Prosecutor from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Your Honour, can I indicate that we do not oppose this motion. I can put that in writing -- I can file something in writing tomorrow if necessary but I would certainly like to indicate that we don't oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't think it is necessary to file anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Robson, for that. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My colleague, Mr. Neuner will be calling the next witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, will you call your witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next witness is Mr. Dzemal Vuckovic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Dzemal Vuckovic. Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Perhaps while the witness is being led into the courtroom, I have conferred briefly with the registrar this morning about how to later tender a certain volume of bulletins and special information reports into evidence. The registrar has suggested that we put some kind of table in writing to the registrar so that it facilitates him to sign exhibit numbers, if Your Honours allow us that these documents are to be tendered into evidence. I just wanted to say this up front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't intend tendering them in a batch as one documents. These are the ones that we were arguing about last week, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is correct. They were all split up by the Prosecution team when the exhibit list was produced in the first place. So each bulletin carries a separate PT number for the time being. There is just one bulletin, 1910, if I remember correctly, which has 500 pages. The Prosecution has checked this exhibit number yesterday, and we, for the time being, do not insist that it is being tendered into evidence. So each bulletin or special information report which is talked about today will carry a separate exhibit number, Your Honours. Separate PT number, Your Honours, I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As and when we get to that stage of the trial and if the documents are admitted into evidence, then they will be done in that most convenient way for the registry to deal with them. May the witness make the oath or the declaration, rather.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, good afternoon, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may sit down --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- and make yourself comfortable. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your name is Dzemal Vuckovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're a Bosniak and you were born in the village of Visici in Capljina and you live currently in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you to statements. Is it correct that you provided in September 2006, a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in November this year, meaning a couple of days ago, you met me in The Hague where had you an opportunity to read your statement and make any corrections and addition to it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can, please, PT6202 be shown to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: After you made these corrections and additions to your old statement, were you signing this statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I only see it now. I signed this statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could scroll down in the B/C/S just to show the signature, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the lower left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And before you signed that statement on the 5th of November, 2007, did you have a chance to look at each document which is mentioned in your statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you carefully reviewed the content of each of these documents. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the content of this second consolidated statement which you signed in the Bosnian language is adequate?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is adequate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to Rule 92 ter, I would like to tender this consolidated statement dating 5 November 2007 with a PT number 6202 and the ERN number, 06143143 till 06143160 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document 6202 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 706.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to show you a few documents now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could, for a second look at Exhibit 669, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the document of the military security service sent to the Military Security Administration of the General Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before we look at some formalities, I just want to show you one passage of it. And this is in B/C/S, the second page. And I'm asking to you look at the second-last paragraph of the second page here. And in English it's page 4, and I'm interested in the third paragraph there. We see here it relates to the battle of Bedr Al-Bosne (Liberating Vozuca the 2nd report) --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I just want to read out a portion of it so that we remember all this document later. It says here in the portion I pointed out to you: "We have taken new territories and new strategic points around Mount Paljenik which we took in the first stage of the operation. The Mujahedin gained ground and entered a group of Serbian villages and took 60 prisoners after the killing." First of all, could you tell me who is reporting this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This report, since it is an original document, was sent to us by the military security department, or, rather, service of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you look at the author of this portion which I just read, if we could scroll in English a little bit up, please, and if you look here what does it say about the line, "Battle of Bedr Al-Bosne"? Who is reporting this information that I just read to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a quoted message from the El Mujahid Detachment to an unknown addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 1, please. The upper part of it. I'm interested in the handwriting in the middle, in the upper middle of that document. Could you explain who made the handwritings here.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the handwritten notes are mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you, with the assistance of the usher who will give you a stylo, encircle those parts of the handwriting which are yours, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could now -- if you could now explain to us what does the letter 03, if I read correctly, in the upper left-hand circle stand for? What did you mean by writing this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the code-name of my department. That is to say, of the analysis department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what does the word next to 03 stand for, which you haven't encircled?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't write that. It says, To be registered. I suppose that the analyst from my department wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go one circle down to the two words which are stricken out, could you explain what the two words mean, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This was the standard practice. When I received a document, I indicated what needed to be done. Apparently, in this case, I decided that a summary of this document should become part of the bulletin. In brackets it says "agreement." This means that the analyst who will receive this document should come over to me to receive instructions from me. However, evidently this report did not become part of the next bulletin because I crossed it out, presumably after having consulted Colonel Popovic who was the chief of the counter-intelligence department, or perhaps even after consultations with General Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what the next circle to the left of the stricken out word bulletin means -- what number did you write down here?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What does 01 stand for?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This means that the document should be sent to the counter-intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the head of that department?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then next to the 01, there's a slash and a number. Could you explain what the slash and number plus the two words next to it, which you haven't encircled, stand for, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I can only assume, since I wasn't the author of these words. I suppose that Colonel Popovic wanted to have this sent to the 3rd section or perhaps this is a code-name of an operative of an officer. Next to it it says code Vranduk. Since this -- at this time operation Vranduk was ongoing, one can prepare that the document was to be treated in accordance with the tasks arising from operation Vranduk.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And below there is a circle, it says: "17 point," and then I cannot really read what does that stand for? Could you explain the last two circles maybe.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And below the 17th of September, we see the last circle on the lower right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Those are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Before I ask that a copy of that document is to be tendered because the witness has made markings on it, could I, for the record, ask that the reference number of that document is being read out or is it not possible now because we have captured the image here as it stands? Maybe I can just tender this copy and then we can move it so we can read the reference. Okay, can I ask to tender this annotated document as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, you may ask. Go on. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 707.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand. You called this document as Exhibit 669 when you called it to the screen. Now, what you are admitting is not Exhibit 669, it is this document but we don't have a name for it. Okay. We just say as annotated. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Annotated, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Exhibit 707?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could move now, since it is an exhibit, the document to see the reference number, please, for a second. It's to the left-hand side of the first document, first page. Okay. Yeah. Just for the record, I would like to read out the reference number. It is 03/ -- one second. 03/1-174223. So I would now like to show you PT2790A. And I ask you to keep the number which is in the transcript in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm afraid the document is not released, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm informed that it is released. We will try to release it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is technology failing us again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm informed it should work now. I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe we can start, since the cover page which is in Bosnian in front of you is relatively easy to translate and I see the Judges get a copy of the English translation already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, Witness, whether you recognise that document, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the main log-book of the administration of military security.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if we look at the third page we have just produced an excerpt out of a lengthy book. If we look at the third page, please, I'm interested in the fourth row from the bottom, and in English it's page 8 of what, hopefully, Your Honours have in front of you now, the sixth column from the top. First of all, I had read the number of the previous document into the record. And I will repeat it to make it easier for you to find the relevant column. It is 03/1-174-223. If you look - and I'm just helping you here now - at the fourth row from the bottom, do you find that number? And in the English it's the sixth column from the top of page -- of page 8.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it, if you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you maybe highlight it so that we are clear which one we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. Vuckovic has marked a vertical line next to the row where he found the reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have only one question for you: Next to the number which is here on the second-last column, which I have read out to you, it says U/PO Vazal. Could you explain to us what that abbreviation means?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That note is a pseudonym of the person whom the military security service treated in an operational manner, in a planned manner and pursuant to an approval of General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who is meant by Vazal?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that that person was from the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment and I think - I'm not sure - that it went for Abu Mali.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you see now here the entry in the log-book, U/PO Vazal what in the context of the document we have seen a moment ago, what does that mean, what is indicated here what is happening to the document which is incoming to the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise to my learned colleague Mr. Neuner. Can we zoom in, because I can't really see a thing. Can we zoom in on this because I can't follow what is being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on this -- yes, we do. Maybe it is even possible to zoom in a little bit further. It is sufficient maybe, yeah. Okay. You're just making a bracket, for the record, of the portion I have read out "U/PO Vazal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Except that it has now disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we now move the document a little bit because it is no longer visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll a little bit? Scroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what does the entry in the last column indicate in relation to the receival of that document, which we have seen a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: The officer noted in the log-book, made notation on which dossier contains this document, where he can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So do you wish to explain that the document, as it went to the Security Administration went to the file Vazal, yeah?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask the that document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that let me just get explanations. The same column on which U/PO Vazal is written has some writing at the bottom that looks like "MUD-SDB." I don't know whether I'm reading that correctly. Are you able to tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one refers to another document, that one a bit -- at the bottom, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then we don't need to know anything about it if it does refer to another document. But then at page 13, line 3, you said, sir, that that note is a pseudonym of the person whom the military security service treated in an operational manner, in a planned manner and purpose in a plan of General Delic. I think there has been a mistype there because I heard you saying that it -- something differently from that. But what I do want to find out from you, first of all, you say, "in a planned manner and purpose" and then what about General Delic? You said it was something like a plan of General Delic, or something like that. And there is no ease on the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this goes for an operational measure that the military security service undertook during the war and for which we had to have an approval given, that it was a measure that required General Delic's approvals. Such subtle measures such as operational processing, actions had to be approved by General Delic. We did not -- we could not, without his knowledge, undertake such measures and this was regulated by our rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did he approve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the operational measure to be taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operative treatment of a person entails collection of all evidence and information about the criminal conduct of such person or inappropriate behaviour or conduct of such a person, if they are a member of the army, with the subsequent aim of collecting documentation and preventing that person from continuing activities against the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And was this person a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That person was formally a member of the army but was not part of the system of command and control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And was that information then collected about this person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was an analyst. This part of operations and actions were conducted by the counter-intelligence department. I remember data intelligence being collected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you remember data intelligence being collected on this person, as a result of this entry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did you see that data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sorry, Mr. Neuner, when I thought I was going ask one question, every answer called for another question. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can -- before -- can you just explain what PO, which is on this document written next to Vazal, what does PO stand for?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a manner of processing. That's previous processing. A person could be processed through previous or preceding processing or operative. Initial processing or previous processing entails that person being monitored to collect intelligence so that that could be moved to a higher degree of processing and that is operative processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So PO stands for initial processing; correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You had indeed asked a little earlier. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 708.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you the next document, PT 2726.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let the record show that the document that is being admitted into evidence is the document on which the witness has made markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, please, PT2726 can be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, I'm interested in the initials, AM, on the lower left-hand side. Could you explain who AM is.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: AM is the author of this document. It goes for an analyst Adnan Muratovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the superior to Adnan Muratovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I was his immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the document is produced by your department. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Head of the department or administration, General Jasarevic signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see the document is from the 22nd of October, 1995, so roughly more than one month than the previous documents were from 16th and 17th of September, and I now wish to look at the second page of that document. We see here a headline, interesting data on activities of some of the heads of the El Mujahedin Detachment. If in English we could also go -- yes, to the second page. And I want to read the first paragraph out to you. It says here: "Military security service of the 3rd Corps has information that the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment command constantly report in writing to their contacts abroad on the situation in the unit and in the battlefield. In one such report, titled, Operation Bosanski Bedr in which the offensive activities of the army units on the Vozuca battlefield were covered, it was stated that the Mujahedin had advanced a lot after killing a large number of Serb soldiers and imprisoning over 60 Chetniks." Could you explain to me what is Mr. Muratovic doing here by compiling this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Muratovic. The witness has said Adnan Muratovic has drafted the document. He is a subordinate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This can be divined from the preceding document that we saw originating from the 3rd Corps where Adnan Muratovic most probably, because beside 03 he put down registered. He entered this, because I presume that his task given by me was to monitor everything that concerned the El Mujahid Detachment and to consolidate, compile and present in a consolidated information or brief. So that was, in other words, the purpose. At the time and given that the operation Vranduk or operational action Vranduk was ongoing and given the subtleness of the measures that were being undertaken during that operation, or operational action, there was a team set up of a certain number of operatives who undertook all the measures and performed the actions that were listed in the plan for the operative action Vranduk, which means that at that moment there was no need from me, as head analyst, to include that in the -- into the bulletin, so that we could have some more time to collect further information on the misconduct of the El Mujahid Detachment and then compile a new report with those included.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You say there was no need to put this into a bulletin. Can I ask you how many times during the war did you learn that 60 POWs had been captured by an ARBiH unit, or a higher number?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall. But this was not my mission anyway, since the tasks from falling under the Vranduk operative action was ongoing, which included technical surveillance, analytical, operative, and other measures including criminal prosecution, so this fell outside of my remitt or my department's remitt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you discuss the issue of the 60 POWs with somebody in your department?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Apparently, I did consult somebody from the management of the military security service, and this is why I crossed out that notation below 03 and wrote down bulletin. It was obviously said to me that this was not to be included in the bulletin but should be part of the report on the Vranduk operative action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who told that you it should not be included in the bulletin but, rather, go to Vranduk?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot, of course, recall now who told me. It could only be General Jasarevic, his assistant Himzo Popovic, Colonel Popovic who was head of the counter-intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 709.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you now to PT2418. First of all, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it. This is the cover page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you explain what type of document is this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: A bulletin is a document containing information for the benefit of readers almost everyday and the readers were the top officials of Bosnia and Herzegovina: First of all, Commander Delic, then President Izetbegovic as commander in chief, and if necessary, the minister of Defence, prime minister, minister of foreign affairs. If it went for issues falling within the remitt, then such information would be forwarded to them as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who produced such a bulletin during the war?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Such documents or bulletins were produced by analysts in the department that I headed, and I verified those, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean by you verified bulletins.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That means when a bulletin is prepared, I would go through it, introduce corrections, if necessary, and send it to the head of the department, Mr. Jasarevic, for him to apply his final verification, and when he verifies such a document, he would be -- it would be made -- copies would be made and sent to the addressees or it would be amended if there were -- needs to be amended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just informed that I have misspelled the number of the bulletin. It is PT2418, for the record. I want to go on and understand what the number 1 means in the upper right-hand side. This is put in in handwriting. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know it. This is the original and it was archived, copies would be forwarded to the recipients. They would be numbered 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 depending on the audience.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we look at the stamp below. Why is the document being stamped?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: For credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If we can enlarge the stamp a little bit for Mr. Vuckovic, please. What I'm interested in if you look at it, there's a 1 in the stamp. Could you explain to us what the 1 stands for, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't really say. I'm not familiar with the administrative matters. Could be that the number noted -- denotes a stamp number 1. There were several stamps; there were smaller ones and larger ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we zoom out again, I want you to look on each page - and we are flipping slowly through the B/C/S side only - and I want to ask you for the -- to look for stamps, if you could just go one page by page. Second page, you see a stamp. You could go to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: There's no stamp on this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could -- and then there's a --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: And there is one on the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that the last page? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So we have seen the stamps, or on one page it was missing. What does the stamp indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Given that these documents were not signed, stamp was supposed to give credibility to the document being sent to the recipients.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If the recipient had an idea or a suggestion based on the information your department provided, what would the recipient do?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand. Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My question is: You're providing information through this bulletin to the limited number of recipient, including Mr. Delic, Mr. Izetbegovic, the minister of Defence. If one of these persons would have a follow-up suggestion based on the information you provided, could you explain what that person would normally do?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That would be a suggestion for General Jasarevic, head of the administration, not for me. If I were to see such suggestions by General Delic, they would be encouraging for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. What I understand and please confirm that, is that if a receiver would have a suggestion, a follow-up issue, then the receiver would contact Mr. Jasarevic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: There was no need for such a thing. Such suggestions were mostly of a morale nature. They would be boosting our morale, they were suggestions that they were supposed to resolve such matters in a military manner. Such suggestions would be of such a nature from Mr. Delic. And I presume that at meetings with General Jasarevic, General Delic would provide concrete, specific suggestions and proposals because, on occasions, General Jasarevic would relay such suggestions to us, of course at briefings and meetings of the security -- military security service administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My last question to that document is: Your analysis section is providing a lot of information here on these three pages. From what sources would your analysis section -- out of which sources would your analysis section compile this bulletin?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: All the secondary documentation, that's to say, bulletins, special information reports, analyses, assessments and so on and so forth, were made based on the reports from the security organs of different corps, of certain divisions that were encircled, such, as for instance, the 28th Division at Gorazde, and on the basis of operative work of the counter-intelligence department which was a constituent part of the Military Security Administration and which also had the task of gathering intelligence. Sometimes we used information we received from different services, most often the state security service with which we had pretty good cooperation, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I note the time, Your Honours. If I could ask the witness -- no, we still have -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at one portion of that document. In B/C/S it's the last page, the second-last paragraph, and in English it's page 3, the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just -- sorry, it's page 3 in B/C/S; I'm not sure that this is page 3. We should, in B/C/S, maybe go one page -- yes. Correct. On the bottom, please, the paragraph on the bottom. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The second-last paragraph if we could just look at this, and in the English it's the second paragraph from the top. Could you, having read the paragraph now, please explain what is the source of that information which your analysis section provides?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: The text says that it's the security organ of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So who, in that security organ of the 3rd Corps, would have the authority to send such a report to your analysis section on the Security Administration level?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This was done by the chief of security of the military security service of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at the very last words of that paragraph, the information your analysis section is providing here states that the El Mujahid Detachment members claim that the matter of cooperation in investigations will be resolved at a higher instance. What does that mean, a higher instance?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Since the detachment was not part of the command and control system, or as we refer to it RiK for short, the term at a higher instance may have meant the entities that they were in touch with that were abroad or it may have been someone higher up in the state. It's very difficult to explain that, but it does confirm that they were indeed outside of the command and control system.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have one point which concerns interpretation, page 25, lines 1 and 2, the witness said quite decidedly that it must have been someone from -- from the political level, so I really want the interpretation to reflect exactly what the witness said. He said someone from the political -- from politics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you also clarify what you mean by "the state," "higher up in the state." Which state are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Are you dealing with Madam Vidovic's problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. Then I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree with the interpretation given by my learned colleague that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you hear what the lawyer said, the lawyer for the Defence said, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, in fact even before Madam Vidovic said that I was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us then clearly what you said in your answer, where they say you're referring to the state. What did you actually say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I can't repeat literally what I said; I can paraphrase. Therefore, this higher instance in my view and I suppose that it could have been in reference to someone from abroad who had been financing them and to whom they reported on their activities or politics, because this detachment, as far as I know, for the entire duration of the war, was not part of the command and control system. That this is in fact true is indicated by the fact that I had never received a single document concerning the military security service or military security of units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina involving this detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that this bulletin, which is bulletin number 161, dated 19th of August, 1995, be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number 710.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the break I would like you to look at Exhibit 377, and especially page 64. And please keep in mind the number of this bulletin I just showed to you is 161. Yes. First of all, I'm interested to learn, if you look at the initials on the lower left-hand side, DzV. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: These are my initials, Dzemal Vuckovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who signed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I signed it upon approval from General Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here you're referring to the bulletin we have just seen, the bulletin number 161, and then you say: "It is necessary to brief Rasim Delic about the contents of the bulletin." And we see that you're sending this to Mr. Sacir Arnautovic in Kakanj. Could you explain what you're doing with this cover letter?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This cover letter clearly shows that Colonel Sacir Arnautovic was in fact in Kakanj, in that period of time, probably on some assignments, and this was an opportunity for me to send this bulletin 161 through Colonel Arnautovic to General Delic, and this was obviously sent by -- or through the packet communication system. In other words, electronically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to, before the break dwell a little bit on bulletins and special information reports. Can you confirm that during the proofing sessions in the last days I have shown you many, many bulletins and special information reports.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And especially on Saturday, but also this morning, did you have several hours to look through each of the bulletins and special information reports I have shown you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I mostly skimmed through them and remembered certain facts contained in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And after you could skim through the documents and remember issues, did you thereafter sign this statement which was admitted this early afternoon?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't sign it today. It was yesterday or the day before yesterday; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I want to find out from you is before you signed your statement, have you had an ample opportunity to look through the bulletins and special information reports which are referred to your statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you confirm that this morning you, again, had an opportunity for more than an hour to look through bulletins and special information reports?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the break, I would like to ask the witness to have a look at the binder during the break, to look at the special information reports and my question to you is whether you could, by browsing through this binder confirm that each of these bulletins are authentic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I have already signed, confirming that the authenticity of daily bulletins and special information reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But I'm particularly interested in those bulletins which are in this binder, just we go for half an hour break now, if you could just look through the binder and tell us after the break whether you find that the bulletins and special information reports are indeed authentic. Could do you that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Gladly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My learned colleague has the binder I handed it out to the Defence before entering the courtroom today. If the Defence could please give the witness the binder and if you please look at the documents and we make a break for half an hour now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time? Okay. We'll now take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you had a chance to go through the binder?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that each bulletin or special information in that binder was produced by your analysis department of the Security Administration of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you also confirm that each bulletin contained in this binder has a stamp on it, stamps on its pages?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you therefore confirm that each bulletin or special information report is authentic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I with these explanations ask that the bulletins contained in this binder are being tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The bulletins contained in the binder are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The bulletins numbers 46 and all will be Exhibit number 711 through Exhibit 757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, let -- let's get -- it's clear, this is not Exhibit 377; this is something else. Because you had you pulled out Exhibit 377 earlier which is still, I think, on the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Correct. This exhibit we are done with. I was referring to the bulletins and special information report in front of the witness right now and the witness could look at it during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I think he did look at them. So we'll say that the binder of bulletins will be Exhibit -- Exhibits --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 711 through 757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. 711 to 757. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just for the record, there are also some special information reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just want to correct the record, I misspoke earlier I said two exhibits 708, I introduced Exhibit 708 with the PT number 2790A, but it should have been 2970A. So I repeat that the Exhibit 708 should have been introduced with a PT number 2970A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examination by Madam Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Vuckovic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My name is Vasvija Vidovic and I will be examining you on behalf of the Defence for General Rasim Delic. The nature of cross-examination is such that most of my questions will be requiring a yes or no answer from you. However, should you feel that your explanation could help clarify some facts, you are invited to give such an explanation.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My questions will have to do with your testimony here and with the documents you have just been shown, as well as the documents you have been invited to comment upon today. In your statement, in paragraphs 13, 14, and 15 you describe the remitt of work of the Security Administration of the Supreme Command staff. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You described the departments within the Security Administration of the staff of the Supreme Command, including your own department. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You described the reporting chain within the military security service. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please make a short pause between my question and your answer in order for the transcript to reflect what we are saying and I'm you asking this because we speak the same language.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the organs of the security service existed in lower level units. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm referring to battalions, brigades, divisions, and corps. And is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As a rule, the organ of the military security service of a lower level command would report to the corresponding organ of an immediately superior command on matters concerning military security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In paragraph 27 of your statement, you described that the Security Administration of the staff of the Supreme Command received reports from corps departments. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: However, at the same time, you said that these departments were fully within the command -- or under the command of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In order to elaborate on these matters for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I should like to ask you the following. It is true, is it not, that in the course of 1992, the rule governing the work of the military security service of the armed forces was enacted, was passed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In its work, the military security service had to adhere to this particular rule at all levels. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: That rule governed and defined the remitt of the military security service. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It regulated its missions and tasks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Tasks and competence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Tasks and competence, that's correct? Tasks and competences?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It also regulated the control and command over that service. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please may Exhibit 585 be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In your statement, you mentioned this rule, and you also mentioned it today, asked by the Prosecutor. And this what you see on the screen is that rule of service, rules of operation for the military security service in the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And a member of the military security service you know that this rule was adopted by the Presidency in September 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: These rules of operations of -- for the military security service in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was being applied throughout the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: By all means, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we show page 6 in the B/C/S version and page 5 in the English version to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, take a look at paragraph 2, control of the military security service. And please pay attention to items 8 and 9, because I'm going to ask you questions about these.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Item 8 regulates that members of the military security service shall be directly subordinated to the commanding officer of the command, staff, unit or institution in which they serve. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is correct and this is what I stated in my written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this is why in paragraph 27 of your statement you say: "Although departments of security service within corps were autonomously -- autonomous in terms of operations, they were under full command of the corps commander," and this is how you explained this rule. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now let us take a look at the next page of this document. Item 11 is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, this is the last item in the -- on the page in the English version and in the B/C/S version this is on the next page. Could you scroll down the English version so that item 11 is visible, please. Right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, please, take a look at item 11. Do you agree that this item states that officers of the military security service in a superior command or staffs, shall, those officers, I mean, shall control members of the military security service of subordinate commands and staffs in technical matters that they shall assist, organise, direct and coordinate their work?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is how it functioned in practice. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, please, take a look at the last several words in item 11. It says there: "Officers of the military security service in a superior command or staffs, shall control their work. So, in other words, officers of the superior command of military security service control the work of subordinate commands in terms of military security. Am I right in saying that this is how the rule specified?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Well, now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On technical matters only. Is it on technical matters only?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are talking about professional matters. Your question was interpreted into as technical. Well, in -- I apologise, but it was interpreted very vaguely into our language, your question, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, did you grasp the gist of His Honour's question and answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can repeat -- I can repeat myself. I'm asking is this in technical matters only and the reason I ask so is because paragraph is 11 says: "Officers in the military security service in superior command shall in technical matters control" ... So I want to know whether this is limited to technical matters only. And I'm saying so, Madam Vidovic, because your last question, before I interrupted, you had said -- yeah, said: "So in other words, officers of the superior command of military security service control the work of subordinate commands." So I wanted to say controlled technical work. Okay? Are we agreed that is how the rule goes, say?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witnesses, Please, I'm going to once you once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But let me -- I want him to answer my question, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am very worried by the interpretation. Your question referring to technical matters in Bosnian really when interpreted doesn't mean a thing. And this is why neither the witness nor I can understand it and we have real problems with the translation and interpretation. In original it says professional matters or professional issues. And this is not the gist of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you permit me, Your Honours, when it refer -- reference is made to technical matters, this I construe as to mean operative techniques or technics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The issue is if the translation of paragraph 11 is the same -- is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, no. And I'm very grateful for your focussing on this. This is not our translation. This is a document procured by the Prosecutor, and the term "technical" as the witness has testified, has a different meaning. But let us clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please explain the essence of item 10. Could you read it? I correct myself, item 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just tell us what is says in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bosnian, it says in professional aspects, which means -- shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please, because that was going to be my next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In professional terms, which means to take measures and actions primarily operative measures or actions or to put it more simply, whether a person or a security concern should be the target of certain measures falling within the remitt of the military security, and, of course, what kind of measures should be taken. Ranging from operative measures to criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what confuses me, Witness. When you now say: "Ranging from -- from operative measures to criminal prosecution." I would have thought that if it says they shall control their professional work, it means that they control the work they do in the furtherance of military security services. But now when you talk of criminal prosecution, that sounds to me a disciplinary matter, which doesn't fall within their work. It looks like it is something that would fall to be controlled by the command -- command of the unit to which they belong. Am I wrong in thinking so?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in a couple of minutes time I'm going to be dwelling on those matters as regulated by this rule and this is what I anticipate to clarify with the witness with your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness we are going to revisit this issue of criminal prosecution -- criminal proceedings and procedure. But what I'd like to ask you is: Everyday engagements of members of military security had to be compliant with the provisions of these rules. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you questions on portions of your statement where you provided testimony of the remitt of the work of the Military Security Administration of the General Staff. In paragraph 24 of your statement you describe that the Security Administration of the Supreme Command staff received documents from corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then in paragraphs 25, 26, 29, 30, 31, and 32, you describe how the Security Administration of the Supreme Command staff functioned. Security Administration, as far as I could grasp, and please correct me if I'm wrong, established such a system whereby documents which would be received from corps would be received at the head's office?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that they would be distributed to departments pursuant to their competencies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Head of administration would, as far as I could divine, personally peruse the documents and issue missions and tasks to departments. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In connection with the content of documents he would undertake concrete or specific steps or activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He would issue orders to commands of military security service. This means his own administration and also orders aimed at departments of military security service at corps level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To them, he would issue directions and he was -- it was incumbent upon him to direct their work. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At this moment, Your Honours, could document D633 be shown to the witness, please. D633. And I will be revisiting the one presently displayed on the screen. Witness, please, this is a brief document. Could you please take a look at its contents and for the benefit of the transcript, I'm going to state that this is a document by the Supreme Command staff of the Armed Forces, dated 10th December 1993. It is entitled: Tasks, and it is addressed to the 3rd Corps command military security sector chief. Are you familiar with this signature?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm the author of this document and it was signed by General Jasarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This document is addressed to the 3rd Corps command. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it is entitled: Tasks?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: By this document, administration head refers to an earlier information that he received from security service of the 3rd Corps and refers to the date of the 4th of December, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And there he says that the information contained in your report concerning Gerila and El Mujahid Detachment that they are important, they merit special attention and that they are indicative because, as it says, it reflects that some foreigners are members from the Muslim brotherhood and demands that the 3rd Corps command take all measures with respect to that. Unfortunately, in the B/C/S we have a black line. But do you agree that it also reads that, please bear in mind the position of the Supreme Command staff commander who, on the 9th of December, 1993, was sent to the 3rd Corps commander, or sent in writing. And further down it says that reports on all new information should be sent promptly. And now, you will agree with me, won't you, that this document is an example of how the security -- military security service functioned in practice. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's so. I very well remember this document, because I authored it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will have to repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You said that you recalled the document. Let me go back several questions. I asked you the following. This document is an example of how the work of the military security service looked like in practice. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can see that in the specific problem involving Gerila and Gerila El Mujahedin, the Security Administration was informed about it from the security organ of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In connection with this problem, it is evident that the Security Administration processed the problem, and issued certain tasks to the department of the military security service of the 3rd Corps? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and this happened on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: As part of the remitt of the -- of the Military Security Administration, on any specific problem it was supposed to issue instructions and tasks to a lower level military security service. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In accordance with the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Furthermore, the task of the Security Administration was to give suggestions to the staff of the Supreme Command on how a certain issue was to be resolved. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on how a certain issue was to be resolved?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But only in those cases in which the commander or the General Staff were competent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In fact I was referring only to those matters that fell within the competence of the Supreme Command and we will get back later to the sensitive processing that you were involved in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask that you pause while the witness is answering, Madam Vidovic, because I think you are overlapping. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'll kindly ask you the following. Please remember the date of the 9th of December, 1993, referred to in this document, where the document mentions this position that was presented by the commander of the Supreme Command staff and that was sent to the commander of the 3rd Corps on the 9th of December, 1993. I will have a question to put to you about this at a later stage. Right now, Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 758.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In this document, we saw that the -- the command that was superior to the organ of the -- of the military security service was issuing instructions to it. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If the chief of the Security Administration believed --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said: Yes, that's correct. Can this witness's answer be entered into the record? The witness confirmed that that was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please repeat your last answer?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If the chief of the Security Administration believed that some other department of the General Staff should deal with a particular matter, and not only the Security Administration, that particular document would be forwarded to the relevant department. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The commanding officer of the Security Administration, that's to say, the chief of the Security Administration, had within his discretion to decide about -- on what matters he would inform other departments of the staff of the supreme command and on what matters to inform the commander of the staff of the supreme command. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My next question will have to do with the bulletins shown to you by the Prosecutor today at the end of his examination-in-chief. You confirmed their authenticity. However, now I want to ask you the following. The Prosecutor didn't show you the originals of these bulletins, did he? You only saw their photocopies. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: These photocopies enabled you to look at photocopies of stamps. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Therefore, you did not review the original bulletins, so it was not on that basis that you could establish whether the photocopies shown to you by the Prosecutor corresponded to the originals of the documents which are filed in the military security service. And that's right, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Only if you reviewed the originals of the bulletins and special information reports and not their photocopies, and if you then compared them with the photocopies shown to you by the Prosecutor, only then would you be able to confirm that those were indeed photocopies of the originals. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I did not have occasion to see the originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When it comes to these originals --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like the witness to have a look at Exhibit 710 that the Prosecutor showed him. Exhibit 710.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm interested in page 1 and I will have questions about that page. Earlier today --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 1 of the Bosnian version back on our screens. Can you show us the first page in the Bosnian version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Today the Prosecutor asked you what number 1 meant --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, I'm referring to this witness's evidence on page 21, line 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- where you said copy number 1 is the original copy which stays in the archives. Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away now. I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 376.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, my understanding is that on the basis of number 1, you concluded that this could be the original copy of this document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. This is a document from the staff of the Supreme Command Security Administration dated the 22nd of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please see the signature block in the B/C/S version. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is an order about the way in which the bulletins and special information reports are to be delivered, the ones from the Security Administration, and it is stated that they should be made in five copies. Look, it says here, copy number 1, is in fact intended for the president of the Presidency. Copy number 2, for the commander of the staff. And you will agree that copy number 5 is intended for the archives. Do you allow for the possibility that you overlooked the existence of this order?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I -- my memory obviously failed me in this regard and I made a mistake in stating earlier on since copy number 5 was the one that was archived. Copy number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
