utterances.text: I would like to us look at another document that you were shown before. And that's Exhibit 377. If this is page 64, and I mean if that's the page that the witness looked at earlier on, 64. No, this isn't the one, because the other one was delivered personally to Mr. Arnautovic. This is fine, yes. Witness, do you recall testifying about this document? When asked by the Prosecutor, you explained that the document we looked at a moment ago, namely bulletin 161, was sent to Kakanj KM, with the contents and it says that the army general should be briefed on the contents of that particular bulletin. And it is General Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt? Madam Vidovic, you called for Exhibit 377. Is this it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document here?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Because when you called for Exhibit 377, a document dated 30th of December, 1995, came up. Was it the wrong document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a set of documents. It's a large exhibit containing this one page that is relevant to me, which is page 64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That makes -- okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, this bulletin, 161, was sent to Kakanj, so that the commander of the General Staff may be informed about it. Would you accept that you were not in a position to know whether Mr. Arnautovic had indeed briefed General Delic on this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot know about that. It's only natural. Besides, my attention was always focussed on my department and on performing all my tasks in a timely manner. Of course, in the absence of General Jasarevic I was the one signing the document, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good. You were not in a position to know whether the General was there at that point in time or whether the document was sent to General Hadzihasanovic who was standing in for him perhaps at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. My obligation ceased the moment the document was sent. From that point on, I didn't know anything else about it, nor was I interested in knowing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I will have several other questions for you concerning reporting. At the moment, I would like the witness to be shown P2078. This is one of the documents that was part of the binder that the learned friend from the OTP showed to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not aware of its exhibit number, Madam Vidovic, because that binder now has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 731, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I failed to note it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please take a look at the last page on this document. The last page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to point your attention to the fact that it is the penultimate page in the English version. The preceding page in the English version, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please, this document discusses the matter of the desecration of a Catholic graveyard and as possible perpetrators reference is made to members of the El Mujahedin Detachment. What I'd be interested in and, of course, there is a reference about another incident at the Zeljezno Polje, if can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I would be interested in as follows. Please read the sentence somewhere in the middle of this document and I'm going to quote it. "Military Security Service, in cooperation with the state security service of Zenica is working on identifying the perpetrators." And also please take a look at the last sentence here. This would be the next page in the English version, please. We have the right page of the Bosnian version but we need the next page of the English version. And it says here: "The Military Security Service is working on finding the perpetrators of this explosion and to this aim, it is assessing information about the conduct of the members of a unit belonging to the El Mujahedin Detachment which has its base in this village." And now, in connection with this, I would like to ask you the following. Recipients - I'm talking about in principle, I'm not going to discuss this specific event - I'm asking about the principles of reporting and action taken in response to these bulletins. Would you agree with me that the recipients of this bulletin, whoever they may be, would understand from the bulletin that the Military Security Service is already taking all measures following within its competence. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it can be seen that perpetrators -- it is -- work is ongoing on identifying the perpetrators which had not been identified up to that point. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that if, in this bulletin and in the other bulletins that you had occasion to see, bore reference that the Military Security Service is undertaking measures, et cetera, then recipients would not necessarily be in a position to instruct or issue certain measures to be taken. Would you accept that as a fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's perfectly clear. This would be within the competences of those organisational units of Military Security Service or the subordinate units of the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Such reference in bulletins and special information reports would be a signal to the recipients of those documents that issues are being resolved. Isn't that so, that they are being worked on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now could the witness be shown, please, document D634.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to dwell on this -- on these questions concerning the principles of reporting within the Military Security Service, a couple of minutes more, and I'm invoking document D634. Please take a look at this document. Do you agree that this is a document of the Military Security Service administration dated 15th of May, 1995, that it is entitled: New information on the conduct of individual members of the El Mujahid Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document is addressed to Fikret Muslimovic personally?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which means that the head of administration of Military Security Service, that he assessed that this issue ought to be resolved by the department for morale. This was his estimate of the situation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you take a look at the end of this document, please. Witness, please take a look at this note at the very end. The Military Security Service has been working to identify those who set off the explosion including checking of information on the conduct of members of a unit of the El Mujahid Detachment and in connection with this incident, it is also stated that the Military Security Service is working to detect the perpetrators. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. With the indulgence of Their Honours, may I explain? Apart from the El Mujahedin Detachment, there were other paramilitary groups of foreigners who had perpetrated criminal offences and often security organs would ascribe such criminal offences to El Mujahedin Detachment members. I will give you an example. The murder of Dr. Zenajid, and I can't recall his family name, near Konjic. That murder was perpetrated by foreign nationals, who frequently were among humanitarian organisation's activities but also acted as armed paramilitary groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I explain. The witness very simply and clearly, in the clearest and simplest possible terms, describes this situation. However, on page 52, lines 2 to 8, transcript does not reflect what the witness is stating in very simple Bosnian terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, Witness I'm going to resolve this matter through my questions. Witness, do you agree that you just said that apart from the El Mujahedin Detachment there were other paramilitary groups who perpetrated criminal offences. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That is what I said, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Also, you cited an example of the murder of a doctor or a physician, and also you said that -- that actions of other paramilitary groups were ascribed to the El Mujahedin Detachment members. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this frequently was not the case. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is what we established subsequently. Our sources, our operative sources, if they saw the perpetrator wearing a beard, they would ascribe that criminal offence to the El Mujahedin Detachment. There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this explanation. And for this reason the Military Security Service sought that perpetrators be identified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You will agree with me, won't you, that was not a simple task concerning that we -- that they had to deal with such people, I mean Arabs and by this I mean it was difficult for both police and Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, it was difficult. I had pre-war experiences when it comes to extremists or similar structures, and I know that this is a very difficult and very responsible task.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain your experience, because I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it relevant, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is, Your Honours, for the Defence, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you mentioned, it was difficult to detect the funders and the perpetrators of criminal offences, which were part of a framework of any extremist activity. This is what I meant by my words.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I'm not going to dwell on this any longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now I want to understand. Are these funders and perpetrators of criminal offences before the war, that's your pre-war experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. At this point, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 759.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, could you take a look at document D635, please. Please, Witness, do you agree that this is a document by Military Security Service administration dated the 10th of July, 1995, and it also deals with threats from members of the El Mujahedin Detachment to soldiers of the 328th Brigade. And do you agree that in this case as well, this information was delivered to the morale guidance administration to the brigadier general Fikret Muslimovic. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the document shows that the General Jasarevic assessed that this issue ought to be dealt with by the morale -- morale guidance administration and that he advised that administration of this. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at the penultimate sentence. And do you agree it reads: "In cooperation with the RiK, or command and control organs, the Military Security Service is taking measures to resolve this problem."

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Therefore, it is concluded that the problems are being dealt with by Security Administration, that measures are being taken. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This is a document authored by my department and the author was Adnan Muratovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 760.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Describing the work of the administration in paragraph 21 of your statement, you explain that you would have morning briefings with the head of your administration, where you would be handed down tasks and missions and where you would inform your superior head of administration, of your work. And you say that minutes of such briefings would be taken. I'm going to revisit those minutes at a later point. But now I would like to ask you something else. I would like to work on the issue that was of interest of His Honour Judge Moloto and that concerned involvement of military security in criminal prosecutions. Do you recall that you confirmed to us that the Military Security Service administration in professional terms controlled and managed the work of subordinate organs and that after -- and this is what you state in paragraph 31 of your statement. By saying that General Jasarevic would issue instructions and orders to military security departments at corps level and also you state that, in this very same paragraph 31 of your statement, you also say that chief of Supreme Command staff did not need an approval to issue instructions to his subordinate organs and units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You explained also in paragraph 31 that the authorisation of the commander of the staff of the Supreme Command was required for the chief of administration at a point when the Military Security Service was supposed to apply special methods and resources which normally encroach upon the constitutionally guaranteed rights of citizens. Do you understand my question? The authorisation issued by the commander of the staff of the supreme command was required by the Military Security Administration only when it came to sensitive matters which encroached upon constitutionally guaranteed rights, such as wire-tapping, surveillance and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Covert monitoring --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This did not, of course, mean that in giving that authorisation the commander would also authorise the institution of criminal proceedings or the start of criminal prosecution. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe we will be revisiting the issue of criminal proceedings after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And before we take the break, this very last question that you asked seems to contradict what the witness specifically says in his statement at that very paragraph, 31. At paragraph 31 he says: "Only on very sensitive issues like if somebody should be criminally prosecuted, he would need an approval from Rasim Delic." But think the last question you asked suggests the contrary, ma'am. Can we deal with that when we come back. Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a moment, please. It seems to me that the Prosecutor did not supply you with the corrected version of the witness's statement, because the witness corrected this, and I'm referring to paragraph 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. I concede that this may not necessarily be the consolidated statement that has been uploaded this afternoon. Can we have a look at that paragraph when we come back. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then we'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe we left off at paragraph 31 of the consolidated witness statement. If you deem it necessary, we can show the witness paragraph 31 of his statement in the Bosnian version. Can the witness be shown PT6202. Can we also have the corresponding page of the English version on the screen, please. It starts on page 6 of the English version. Your Honours, I'm referring to the consolidated statement. I should like the witness to look at the bottom part, starting with: "The authorisation of Rasim Delic." In English, it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'll quote this, witness, so that we can confirm that this is indeed the part of the statement that I referred to previously. Paragraph 31, in the section where it says: "Only on very sensitive issues such as, for instance, commencing operative treatment of a person, commencing operative activities or the use of special methods and measures vis-a-vis a person, surveillance, monitoring, et cetera, he would need an approval from Rasim Delic. My -- for all the issues that my department dealt with, orders could be given without the authorisation of Rasim Delic." Therefore, it was only for these special methods that General Delic needed to give his authorisation to the Military Security Service, for its work. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have a question for this witness. If I'm not mistaken, what I see here is that in this paragraph you make reference to activities which, to my mind, seem to be activities of the security department -- department. Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are activities of the military security department. However, according to the rules governing the Military Security Service, for such a subtle activity as -- as is covert surveillance, monitoring, listening in and so on and so forth, the authorisation of General Rasim Delic was required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. But you think that when it comes to delicate questions in certain sectors you don't mean here all delicate situations or delicate questions. So there could be some other delicate questions, don't you? On the basis of this declaration, am I wrong what delicate questions were there? I want your explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite clearly, not all such activities were listed here, not all such sensitive issues as I refer to them in my statement. Such activities called for an authorisation of General Delic, or, rather, from an army commander, whenever an operative action was to be taken, such as operative action Vranduk team and some other actions conducted by the Military Security Service; or when a certain person or a certain case was to be given operative treatment, which meant taking a broader range of measures and activities with a view to documenting, or, rather, detecting and documenting a criminal activity of a given person; or where a negative activity was to be documented in a group, such as, for instance, Trebevic operative action, where -- which was taken across a wider, a broader territory under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina on several occasions, and I believe that there five or six such operations. In short, such operations required the authorisation of Commander Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that everything you have just explained to the Trial Chamber is specifically regulated in the rules governing the work of the Military Security Administration, that you had occasion to look at previously?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I said that in my early answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well. In order to clarify these matters, I want the witness to look at Exhibit 585.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, could we just ask the witness then what the last sentence in paragraph 31 means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that, or do you want me to read it out for you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that and it's quite clear. Perhaps it's not precise enough. For all operative issues that my department maybe dealing with, orders could be issued without the authorisation from Rasim Delic. This went or applied not only to the Military Security Administration but also to the lower level organs such as those of the corps, division, brigade, they could take measures even without the authorisation of the Military Security Administration, let alone the authorisation from Commander Delic. They could file criminal reports against the perpetrators of offences, of criminal offences.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was just about to deal with this matter, because Exhibit 585 contains these precise rules. So can we please put away the document that we have on our screens right now and look at Exhibit 585. We would like page 10 of the Bosnian version and page 7 of the English version to be shown; namely, chapter 4, pages 10 of the Bosnian and 7 of the English version. Can you zoom in on that exact part. Yes, thank you. Chapter 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that this portion of the document, as you see it, regulates the powers and responsibilities of officers in the Military Security Service in the performance of their duties?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page now, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to draw your attention to Articles 32, 33, and 34 of the Rules of the Military Security Service, which concern the filing of criminal reports for the criminal offences within the jurisdiction of -- of military courts. Before you proceed to read this, Witness, I want to ask you the following. All the criminal offences within the competence of the Military Security Service were in fact criminal offences within the jurisdiction of military courts in times of war. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This included serious criminal offences such as war crimes, murder, and similar crimes. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is quite easily seen in the bulletins where we were informing the recipients of the units which had initiated criminal proceedings against individuals suspected of committing crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please focus on Article 32 and read it. No, please read it to yourself and I will have a question for you. Do you agree that the provisions of Article 32 of the Rules of the Military Security Service clearly regulates that the authorised commanding officers of the Military Security Service can arrest an individual and arraign him before a military court without delay, where there is reasonable doubt to believe that a crime was committed which falls within the jurisdiction of a military court?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. And, as I said earlier, an illustration of Article 32 can be found, or, rather, of its application, can be found in the contents of the bulletins.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Fine. Now, please take a look at the provision of Article 34. Moreover, Military Security Service could order detention for such a person lasting up to three days before delivering that person to an investigating magistrate. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we'd like to take a look at page 13 in Bosnian and page 9 of the English version, a section which specifically regulates the conduct of Military Security Service in criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you confirm that chapter 5 regulates the conduct of Military Security Service in criminal proceedings? And, Witness, please, focus on Articles 40 and 41, because these refer to the gist, the core of our discussion. Please read it to yourself and then I'll ask you questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you scroll up please, in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. 40 and 41. Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you this: Do you agree that the provision of Article 40 regulates that officers of the Military Security Service are duty-bound to take measures to detect and identify perpetrators of criminal offences to detect and secure evidence for the purposes of criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is clearly stated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now please read Article 41. Do you agree that this provision of Article 41 of the rules of operations of the Military Security Service governs that officers of the Military Security Service in the command of the brigade or a corresponding or higher-ranking officer in the Military Security Service submit to the competent military prosecutor's office a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Therefore, please, it is the duty of a military security service officer, be it an officer in a brigade organ or in a corps or in a division, is whenever they receive information about a perpetrated criminal offence, to collect evidence and to submit a criminal report to the competent prosecutor. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are perfectly right in saying so. I'd like to add, though, that it is their duty to collect documents admissible in court apart from information and data.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of course. Thank you very much, Witness. Therefore, it is not incumbent upon them to write information about criminal offences. It is incumbent upon them to collect evidence and to submit a criminal report to the competent prosecution service.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is the original competence deriving from this rule on the operation of Military Security Service and for that they do not need any special approvals. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please, during the war, there were thousands of criminal reports filed with prosecutors in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the part of Military Security Service on the basis of those rules. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: You are right and this can be corroborated in the annexes of numerous bulletins that we issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me also that a criminal report could be filed against persons unknown and in cooperation with competent prosecutor it could be possible to take measures to identify such perpetrators and to collect evidence against them?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So, the rule that we have before us precisely regulated how the Military Security Service should conduct itself in initiating criminal proceedings and no advice, approvals were not necessary to do so. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is right. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you don't have any questions concerning this, we may put this document away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you about another thing concerning your testimony. You discussed how commander of the General Staff would be informed. I'd like to ask you in connection with this the following. The administration that you worked in was in charge of preparing analytical and information materials for the reporting and information of the competent commands of state organs. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In connection with this, your administration could propose necessary security measures and activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your department within that administration that you worked in, sent its reports exclusively to the head of the administration within the General Staff -- no, I apologise, the head of the administration. So you sent your reports to the head of your administration and by this I mean General Jasarevic. I may have expressed my thought incorrectly. Did you understand?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understood. This was the procedure. Whenever my department would prepare a document for the purpose of informing somebody, be it a bulletin or special information report, an analysis, all such documents I delivered to General Jasarevic, who then authenticated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At this junction I'd like to clarify paragraph 33 of your statement. You will agree with me when I say that General Jasarevic decided on what and to what extent he would be informing the commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is correct. And General Jasarevic, if he was present, would note which important information should be forwarded to General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not referring to bulletins; I'm referring to meetings and informations. This is what I'm discussing.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, meetings and information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Now I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How much longer are you going to be? You've taken 1 hour 30 minutes; your colleague took 1 hour 4 minutes. I know he filed a -- bundle of documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will need more time for certain. The Prosecutor has tendered a large number of documents pursuant to 92 ter, and this means I would need more time and I believe that my learned colleagues would be in agreement that I need more time to discuss many documents. If I can be given another hour, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Carry on, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do my best, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You discussed bulletins and special information reports, and you stated that they would be sent to specific addresses. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you concluded your work, when you put a bulletin into an envelope, from that point on, you do not know whether the addressee, be it Commander Delic, President Izetbegovic or the Ministry of Defence, you do not know whether that person received that bulletin or not until it's returned and I'm going to discuss this later on. So if it doesn't bear any comments on it, you do not know whether the bulletin has been read by the recipient or not. Is that correct? I mean that recipient personally.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This was not an issue of my interest and neither did it fall within my job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, you said that some information would be returned bearing a comment in longhand, written by General Delic, and then you would personally conclude that he had read that information report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In paragraph 40 of your statement, you said that documents that would be returned bearing comments, which would include Mr. Delic as a recipient, were destroyed. Do you recall stating so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would you accept that it is possible that those documents were not destroyed or partially destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Because being short of paper, even such documents were archived sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, was your question like that, as it appears on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is missing is a small part. My question was: Would you accept that after all, all these documents, all, were not destroyed. The word "all" was missing. That was my question, Your Honours. I cannot really keep an eye on the transcript and what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question, Witness? My question was, would you accept that all documents that were returned annotated in longhand were not destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said just now. Sometimes being short of paper, we did not produce a copy for our purposes but would archive a copy, annotated or returned by the commander or some other recipient and in this way, we would save paper. We did not have much paper during wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So I understood --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just ask one question. Now all documents which were returned without having been annotated in longhand, what became of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were destroyed because they were surplus. They were not needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now, in your testimony, you mentioned written notations of General Delic, and from that, I conclude that you are able to recognise such notations. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I most probably would be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we show, Your Honours, document D636 to the witness, please. This is the same document as P1640, but it's not annotated in longhand and both originate from the documentation of the OTP. I decided to use this one which bears a note, handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that this is a special information report? And could we zoom in on the handwritten note. This is a special information report, number 234, dated -- and at that time when this was produced, you were in -- an analyst in the department of military security. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the last page of this document to see the signature block.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, that's page 3, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise this. This is General Jasarevic's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at page 2 of the document. Page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Towards the top, please take a look and see -- please take a look and what is written at the bottom of the document where it describes sector of military security of the 3rd Corps. Can you confirm that this special information report concerns the conduct of foreign citizens in the area of responsibility of the 3rd -- of the corps and concerns the units of Gerila and Mujahedin. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The portion -- can you please read that portion of the text.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This part of the text contains a suggestion of the Military Security Service to the recipients of this special report that without any delay, they should prevent the criminal conduct and war profiteering carried out by some of these individuals. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Let us go back to page 1 of this document. I want to draw your attention to the handwritten annotation. Would you agree with me that this annotation has two parts, or, rather that it's been written, so it seems by two different individuals?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone's signature, anyone's handwriting, rather?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the handwriting at the top is by Commander Delic and that the handwriting of the bottom part of the text is by analyst Husnija Sajdinovic and I do recognise his handwriting; we used to work in the service together before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you read the top annotation which was written by, as you say, General Delic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that it reads: If that is indeed the conduct as described herein, it should be sorted out militarily?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be admitted into evidence, because the copy attended by the Prosecution does not have this handwritten annotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number 761.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In your evidence, you said that you saw annotations written by Commander Delic in various documents. Please, Witness, were these annotations of the same nature such as this one? Were they in the form of an order aiming at resolving problems, rather than covering them up?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is quite evident. In addition to such -- in addition to such annotations General Jasarevic would convey to us during the morning briefings we had similar instructions that he had received from General Delic, such as, for instance, when the implementation of operative action Vranduk was discussed, we were told that this should be the priority of the Military Security Service. Therefore, General Delic insisted that this action, or, rather, that the implementation of the measures arising from this action, be the priority task of the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away now. On the same topic, I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 690.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, before you take a look at the document, do you remember me asking you to commit to your memory the date which was in fact a handwritten annotation on one of the documents mentioning the order of General Delic and some sort of -- his position. This was a document dated the 10th of December, 1993, number 758 where General Jasarevic issued tasks to the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you remember me asking you to remember the date of the 9th of December, as the date of the document wherein General Jasarevic told the Military Security Service to keep in mind the position of the commander of the Supreme Command in resolving these matters. This position that was contained in a written document. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please look at this document now dated 9 December 1993, tasks for further crackdown on illegal activities in the ARBiH units addressed to the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please scroll down the document, or, rather, can we see the entire document for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe you had this document in mind when you were writing that document. I believe you said you authored that document we looked at a moment ago. Is this the document you had in mind? Have a look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that the position of the commander of the staff of the supreme command is quite unequivocal here. He is asking to apply all available measures in order to make sure that units are placed under control?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And that if this is impossible, the units should be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to the next page of this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the units discussed in this document are the units called Gerila, Mujahedin and El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Similarly, at the end of the document, it is stated: Keep us duly informed on the course of assign the tasks and if you encounter any serious difficulties. Do you agree with me that that handwritten order by Commander Delic that you saw in that document referred to this written document concerning the Gerila, Mujahedin and El Mujahedin units?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In fact, it is true that General Delic had fully accepted the assessment provided by the chief of the Military Security Administration and supported his opinion that all available steps should be taken in order to make sure that these units are placed under the control and command of the army, and if this should prove to be impossible, that they should be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been aware of this even without looking at the document, since I was present at the meetings when Commander Delic would tour the various departments, including the Military Security Administration, where he presented his positions, I can say that they are identical to the positions presented in these -- in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I get help here. Does the B/C/S version talk of if something is impossible, they should be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure of the term destroyed, Your Honours, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's my concern because I don't remember seeing it on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In putting the question to the witness, no, I didn't use the term "destroy." I used a term "clearing up" or something like that, perhaps it was misinterpreted, to clear up. In fact, could we have page one of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What would clearing up mean anyway?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, let us go back to that. The document speaks clearly about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, look at paragraph 1 and I will quote that part. It will be faster and clearer. The document says: "With the aim of successfully carrying out the decisions of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the orders of the staff of the Supreme Command on dealing with illegal activities in the units of the army, as well as the behaviour that endangers unified and flawless functioning of the command and control system, take necessary measures without delay and in a proper manner to resolutely stamp out such problems in the units that are mainly comprised -- that are exclusively or mainly comprised of foreign nationals." Witness, you heard what His Honour asked. What does this resolute clamp-down mean?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: In the Bosnian language, it means to clarify, to make more precise, to gather fresh information, take measures, shed light on, that sort of thing. This term was normally used by security services and that's why it may be perhaps unclear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Let me be sure I understand you, sir. You say in B/C/S, stamp out or clamp down means clarify, find more information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry, but there seems to be -- there seem to be totally two different tracks in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... Ask interpreters to help us to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't -- the interpreter was still talking and I didn't hear what she said. I'm sorry. It's not even there on the screen now. Sorry, what were you saying, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was saying that there seem to have been problems in interpretation both ways. If you'll allow me, I will try to clarify this with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that the B/C/S term "rasciscavanje" means to clarify a matter, to take measures in order to clear the matter up, to sort it out, to, in fact, solve a problem?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where it says to sort the matters out with a given unit, this means to either put it in the right order or to disband it. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: To disband what? To disband the problem? That phrase, to disband it, doesn't -- I don't understand what it means now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was saying to disband a unit but it wasn't interpreted. This is what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said to disband it. Did you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to disband a unit. That's what I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is that right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: In the security services, this term implied also to gather information, to clarify matters and to take measures to neutralize unlawful activities in various ways through criminal Prosecution, disciplinary measures and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm terribly sorry but I really must ask the interpreters one thing. I don't want to philosophize here or to just have a loose interpretation of words. I would like to know what that word means. One word what does it mean. I would like to know what is the translation of one word not by a sentence. I would just like to know what that word means. Thank you. Maybe the interpreters did not understand which word. For me it's a bit difficult for me to read it out. It is "rasciscavanje." I believe that that is the word that Madam Vidovic is referring to. I'm only talking about that one word.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The practice for the interpreters to refer Their Honours to the official translation from the relevant service, the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. And I hope that the English booth gave the same translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Clear up, to clarify. It may also mean to sort out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, you worked in security services, and you just mentioned operations approved by General Delic. You mentioned operation Trebevic and you said there were four or five operations code-named Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I think there was six.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Six, okay. Do you recall, to the best of your knowledge, that Trebevic-3 concerned the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Trebevic-4 concerned the municipalities of Travnik, Visiko and Zenica. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that this was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Finally, you said that in May 1995, General Delic approved the operative action known as Vranduk?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This was a code-name for that, Operation Vranduk.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Fine. You discussed that in your statement in paragraph 59 and I'm not going to ask you extensively about that. But I would like you to be shown another document, Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Exhibit 662. This is an exhibit under seal, so whether -- therefore I'd like to seek that we sit in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we can put this document away. And could we show the witness Exhibit 669, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You commented on your -- on this document in paragraph 57 of your statement. And today you asked [as interpreted] Prosecution questions, you may remember that you made circles around your handwriting on this document. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you replied that this annotation bulletin was crossed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This simply means that this information was not included in the bulletin. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is clearly visible here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Right. Below that, what is written is code-name Vranduk. I would like to ask you about a principle when it comes to operative activities and investigations and delivery of information on such activities. Please, do you agree with me that Vranduk was an activity which entailed criminal investigations, among other things?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. This is perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well. Please, do you agree that when it came to investigative activities, then state organs are duty-bound to be mindful of protection of such information. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This means, please, that regardless of who -- of who is the recipient, when operative investigations and criminal investigations are concerned, such information would not be included in bulletins. These are protected information for the purposes of investigations. Am I correct in saying so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this was the real reason why it was decided that this information should not end up in the bulletin and this is why the word bulletin was stricken through?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was so, because of possible leak of such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So this would not concern only this information, but any other information that would jeopardise operative activities or, in other words, investigations, such information would not end up in special information reports or bulletins. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is perfectly evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we put this document away. At this point I would like the witness to see P2871.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honours. I thank you. 2871.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a document dated 30th of December, 1995, another document of the Military Security Service administration addressed to the General Staff command post of Kakanj and in this specific instance it was addressed to Captain Enver Berberic. We saw a similar situation where this document was addressed to Sacir Arnautovic. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So any situation when the document is sent to Kakanj, you no longer know of its fate, whether it gets delivered to General Delic or somebody who stands in for him if he is absent?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: My duty is performed when I receive from the communications centre that the document had been sent, and after that I really don't care.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you concerning paragraph 49 of your statement. The Prosecutor asked you whether a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment was target of criminal prosecution. You answered that you did not know. Now, Your Honours, I would like to see this document be put away and to -- witness be shown document PT1686.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't want this document admitted, ma'am? Or is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are the documents either shown to the witness by the Prosecutor or which are part of the binder which are going to be admitted. I'm referring to them as under P numbers because I don't know at this point what exhibit numbers they are going to be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, and that's why I asked once you referred to it under a number P and -- because I also don't know, I assume it's a new document which needs to be given an Exhibit number. And I don't want your exhibits to slip through the fingers and not be admitted, Madam Vidovic. So I am doing this out of an abundance of caution to make sure that documents referred to are tendered if they are intended to be tendered. Thank you very much. Exhibit 757, I am told.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That's 757.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown document 1686, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest that if it comes from the binder, do say so, then we know it is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is Exhibit 716.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. But if Madam Vidovic says it comes from the binder, then we know it's admitted and you don't have to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This goes -- bulletin number 24, dated 31st of January, 1994. Can page 2 of the document be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, please focus on paragraph 2 which starts with the phrase: "At the same time." And can we scroll the English version down so it can be seen. It reads: "At the same time, a joint security service centre Zenica and Military Security Service during their work in realising operational plan of measures and activities in finding the organisers and executors of the killing and wounding of UNHCR members, it found that a vehicle of make Golf with three arrested foreign citizens from Arab countries and we informed in the previous bulletin about their arrest, they were on the day in question at the scene where the killing and wounding of UNHCR members occurred." Later on in the document it is mentioned that there are suspicions that some of them may be members of the El Mujahedin Detachment. In connection with this I would like to ask you this: Reading this bulletin one could conclude there was an investigation conducted on the murder of foreigners committed by foreign citizens, can be -- can it be concluded -- can we go to the second -- to the next page in the Bosnian version. Or may be committed by El Mujahedin Detachment members?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I do believe that this investigation was operation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It seems that this was being reported on in this bulletin and in the preceding one, judging from what is written here. In other words, you agree that investigations were conducted and criminal reports were being submitted against such members of El Mujahedin or can you correct your previously statement?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the detachments. I don't know which detachment those members belonged to; maybe it is written somewhere in the text. If I were to read the text maybe my memory would be jogged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You may read the first paragraph. Take a look at it, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: It says that most probably these were El Mujahedin detachment members.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you would agree that criminal investigation and criminal -- were initiated and criminal reports were submitted against them?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL VUCKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since I'm about to embark on a sizeable document maybe this would be the right time for me to finish for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic, we'll take a break and actually adjourn to tomorrow at 2.15 in the afternoon. Same courtroom, II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of November, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
